summary: In the United States, Ribavirin carries the Food and Drug Administration's strongest warning for blood harm, breathing harm, and birth defects or damage to unborn babies [3][5]. The drug's warnings also note that it can cause destruction of red blood cells (hemolytic anemia) and may linger in parts of the body for up to six months [5]. According to a small computer model rather than human tests, Ribavirin received a high risk score of 71 for the liver and a low risk score of 21 for the heart [M].
